1.name: Base
1.note: The pump's foundation. Its drillings carry the compressed air from the barrel past the check valve to the hose.

2.name: Tread pad
2.note: Rubber pads you stand on. They keep the base from sliding while you push the handle down.

3.name: Barrel tube
3.note: The cylinder. The piston sweeps 281 cm³ of air through it on every stroke.

4.name: O-ring
4.note: Seals the barrel to the base, so compressed air can only leave through the check valve.

5.name: Clamp screw
5.note: Pinches the split base round the barrel to hold it upright.

6.name: Top cap
6.note: Closes the top of the barrel and carries the rod bushing. It is vented, so the space above the piston stays at atmospheric pressure.

7.name: Rod bushing
7.note: A bronze sleeve that guides the piston rod straight, so the cup seal wears evenly.

8.name: Piston rod
8.note: Carries your push from the handle down to the piston.

9.name: Piston hub
9.note: The aluminium body of the piston. It backs the cup seal on the down-stroke.

10.name: Cup seal
10.note: The inlet valve. Pressure presses its lip against the wall on the way down; on the way up it folds in and lets fresh air past.

11.name: Washer
11.note: Spreads the nut's clamping force over the piston hub.

12.name: Hex nut
12.note: Holds the piston stack on the end of the rod.

13.name: Handle hub
13.note: Joins the T-handle to the rod.

14.name: Handle tube
14.note: The crossbar you push. Your force times the piston area sets the pressure you can reach.

16.name: End plug
16.note: Caps the open ends of the handle tube.

17.name: Check ball
17.note: The outlet valve. It lifts off its seat only when the chamber pressure passes the tyre's, and drops back so the tyre can't leak back.

18.name: Valve spring
18.note: Holds the check ball lightly on its seat between strokes.

19.name: Hose barb
19.note: Screws into the base and grips the hose.

20.name: Hose
20.note: Carries the air from the base to the tyre valve.

21.name: Gauge
21.note: A Bourdon-tube gauge. It reads the hose pressure, which equals tyre pressure whenever the check valve is shut.
